newsitem.title: UK: Major sees UK in pieces if Labour wins.
newsitem.headline: Major sees UK in pieces if Labour wins.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major warned on Monday that victory for the main opposition Labour Party in Thursday's election would provoke the break-up of Britain into bite-sized bits.

Major was speaking on the second leg of a whirlwind tour of the four parts of the United Kingdom to highlight what he sees as the dangers of Labour policy to devolve power to Scotland and Wales and to cede more power to the European Union.
"Before you come to Thursday, do stop and think and pause. Realise what is at stake," Major told a crowd of about 200 in the Scottish capital.
"This may be a vote that you cast that will change the history and future of Scotland and the rest of the United Kingdom. I don't tell you that lightly, I mean that quite literally."

He said with a Scottish tax-raising parliament, "there might be precious little point in sending members of parliament to Westminster (London) for they would be to all intents and purposes without influence and power to act for Scotland there".
He said the need to defend the United Kingdom from breaking up was one of the central issues of our time.
Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, fighting for his political life in the streets of Edinburgh Pentlands, dismissed as nonsense a reporter's suggestion that Major was on a farewell tour of Britain.
He said it was appropriate for Major to carry out a symbolic visit to all parts of the United Kingdom to alert voters to the threat of disintegration that a Labour government would pose.
"The Labour Party's proposals are not only ill-thought out and ill-considered, but they represent the most fundamental change in the way the United Kingdom is governed for almost 300 years."
"In many respects, May 1 is going to be a referendum on the future of the United Kingdom," Rifkind told reporters.
Major earlier visited Belfast and was due to stop in Anglesea, North Wales on his way back to London for a series of television interviews.
